no_target_yet.statement:
For every nonzero $p\in V_3$, the configuration $C_p$ has 31 points, 75 lines,
and contextuality degree 12. If $H\subseteq\LL_3$ has exactly three lines
through each of the 63 ambient points, then $|C_p\cap H|=15$.
In particular, \eqref{eq:conjecture} fails for $C_p$ and every classically
embedded split Cayley hexagon.

no_target_yet.next_step: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.reason: Formalization work is coordinated through the shared requests.
no_target_yet.statement:
For every nonzero three-qubit pole $p$,
\[
 d(A_p)=0,\qquad d(B_p)=d(C_p)=12.
\]
For every classically embedded split Cayley hexagon $H$,
\[
 |A_p\cap H|=3,\qquad |B_p\cap H|=12.
\]
There is an assignment on $B_p$ whose violated lines are exactly $B_p\cap H$,
but no assignment on $C_p$ has that complete violation set.
More generally, deleting the pole pencil preserves the full-perp degree in
every $n\ge2$ qubits: $d(B_p^{(n)})=d(C_p^{(n)})=4d_{n-1}$.
Every minimum-violation assignment on the full perp satisfies its pole pencil.
no_target_yet.title: Counterexamples to Saniga et al.'s line-subgeometry conjecture and fourfold hexagon constructions

For every $U$ and every assignment, there is a vector $w_U\in U$ such
that the affine complement $A_u=\{v\in U:u(v)=1\}$, indexed by
$0\ne u\in U^*$, is violated precisely when $u(w_U)=1$.
Consequently its seven affine contexts have either zero or four violations.
